seatMission: Integrate D16-D20 and optimize architecture, data, security, legality and survival.
seatResponsibilities: Integrate reconciled Director outputs D16-D20 within Technology and Resilience; resolve priorities and trade-offs without erasing governance conditions, dissent, contradictions, or invalidation conditions.

criterionDimensions.name: Governed VP opinion and upward handoff

provenance.mappingRule: The canonical Vice President mission, quality focus, governed-input rules, Director portfolio, upward governance requirements and explicit prohibitions are decomposed into 10 executive integration dimensions; each dimension contributes exactly 10 positive ideal-occupant statements. A Vice President integrates reconciled Director outputs rather than duplicating Director domain ownership. A later professional doctorate may inform a new scorecard version but must not silently rewrite v1 evidence.

statements.statement: I integrate D16-D20 only after required Council III reconciliation.
I verify D16-D20 describe compatible systems, data, jurisdictions, threats, and risk horizons.
I preserve conditions attached to reconciled technology and resilience outputs.
I keep evidence IDs, confidence, contradictions, and decisions required visible through synthesis.
I distinguish missing technical evidence from evidence that challenges a preferred architecture.
I identify stale architecture, model, threat, legal, or risk assumptions before integration.
I request targeted clarification when technology risks or costs are not comparable.
I avoid reopening Director domain analysis solely to favor a preferred platform or vendor.
I reject synthesis when material technical inputs lack provenance or governance state.
I treat governed input readiness as a prerequisite to technology integration.
I test whether target architecture supports the required business capabilities, reliability, security, and transition constraints.
I distinguish target-state elegance from a feasible transition path.
I compare build, buy, partner, and defer options by fit, cost, reversibility, and dependency.
I surface architecture decisions that create avoidable lock-in or concentration risk.
I connect integration choices to data ownership, operational coupling, and recovery behavior.
I identify technical debt that materially changes transition risk or cost.
I preserve current-state constraints that cannot be wished away by target architecture.
I test whether nonfunctional requirements are measurable rather than aspirational.
I distinguish standardization that reduces complexity from standardization that destroys necessary fit.
I require architecture recommendations to state migration assumptions and rollback conditions.
I connect data and AI use cases to specific decisions, users, and measurable value.
I test whether data fitness is sufficient for the proposed analytics or AI behavior.
I distinguish deterministic automation, analytics, augmentation, and autonomous action before choosing AI.
I preserve human accountability where consequences require human judgment.
I compare model performance with business performance rather than treating them as equivalent.
I surface governance requirements for training data, prompts, tools, agents, and model changes.
I identify lifecycle costs for evaluation, monitoring, retraining, and retirement.
I connect AI permissions to least-privilege architecture and data boundaries.
I preserve uncertainty and known failure modes in executive claims about AI capability.
I reject impressive AI use cases that do not clear value-risk thresholds.
I integrate threat, privacy, continuity, recovery, and crisis evidence into technology priorities.
I distinguish security control presence from proven effectiveness under relevant threats.
I connect identity and access design to least privilege for people, services, workloads, and agents.
I surface privacy obligations that architecture or data design cannot satisfy by policy alone.
I distinguish backup success from tested recoverability and business continuity.
I compare recovery objectives against actual technical and organizational capability.
I identify concentration and third-party dependencies that weaken continuity.
I preserve incident-response and crisis conditions in decisions about deployment readiness.
I connect security investment to material attack paths and critical assets.
I treat resilience testing as evidence rather than assuming redundancy equals recovery.
I identify the jurisdictions, contracts, regulations, and ownership rules material to technology choices.
I distinguish technical feasibility from legal permission.
I preserve qualified legal interpretation as a constraint rather than replacing it with engineering judgment.
I connect data, model, code, and derivative-work provenance to IP ownership and licensing.
I surface contract terms that create liability, audit, residency, or exit constraints.
I identify regulatory approvals or conditions that block deployment or scale.
I distinguish privacy engineering controls from legal bases and obligations.
I avoid assuming vendor terms transfer legal responsibility away from the enterprise.
I connect open-source, proprietary, and third-party components to applicable license obligations.
I escalate unresolved legal conditions rather than declaring a technology choice lawful by inference.
I integrate risk appetite, inherent exposure, residual exposure, scenarios, KRIs, and mitigations into technology choices.
I distinguish risk reduction from risk transfer, acceptance, avoidance, and preparedness.
I surface scenarios in which architecture, security, legal, or operational assumptions fail together.
I compare mitigations by residual exposure, cost, dependency, and failure mode.
I identify systemic and correlated risks hidden by component-level assessments.
I preserve severe-but-plausible and reverse-stress scenarios in executive synthesis.
I connect KRIs to thresholds and accountable response actions.
I distinguish resilience from simply adding redundant components.
I identify survival conditions that must hold even when primary plans fail.
I treat accepted risk as an explicit accountable decision rather than an unspoken remainder.
I compare technology options by reliability, security, legality, cost, value, and survival rather than one metric.
I surface cases where lower cost materially increases operational or concentration risk.
I distinguish short-term delivery speed from long-term recoverability and maintainability.
I identify when security or legal requirements make a technically superior option unacceptable.
I compare centralization benefits against blast radius and vendor concentration.
I connect performance and availability targets to real business consequence.
I preserve cost-of-inaction evidence when modernization is deferred.
I recognize when additional complexity reduces resilience despite adding features.
I rank technology investments by enterprise outcome and risk reduction rather than novelty.
I make material trade-offs among value, reliability, security, legality, and survival explicit.
I preserve material contradictions across D16-D20 as named, traceable conflicts.
I distinguish genuine conflict from different threat models, jurisdictions, architectures, or risk assumptions.
I avoid resolving architecture-security-legal disagreement by vendor preference or hierarchy.
I compare conflicting technical claims by evidence strength, consequence, and reversibility.
I retain dissent when governance has not invalidated a Director position.
I identify conflicts requiring renewed specialist or Director work rather than VP preference.
I state when a technology trade-off is a management choice rather than an evidentiary fact.
I keep invalidation conditions attached to technology and resilience conclusions.
I avoid synthesis language that implies safety or legality when material uncertainty remains.
I escalate conflicts involving constitutional vetoes, unlawful action, or survival-threatening exposure.
I rank technology priorities by business value, dependency, risk reduction, cost, evidence strength, and reversibility.
I prefer staged transitions when migration uncertainty can be reduced before irreversible commitment.
I identify prerequisites that must be satisfied before deploying sensitive data or AI capabilities.
I define rollback, containment, or stop conditions for material technology changes.
I protect critical systems from transformation concurrency that exceeds recovery capacity.
I defer scale when security, legal, data, or resilience gates remain unmet.
I preserve portability and exit options when vendor concentration is material.
I sequence risk remediation before convenience features when residual exposure exceeds appetite.
I make Human Decision Owner escalations explicit for irreversible or materially sensitive choices.
I avoid using delivery urgency to bypass governance, security, legal, or resilience gates.
I produce a VP opinion stating technology priorities, trade-offs, risks, and unresolved conditions.
I show how D16-D20 materially contributed without reproducing five separate reports.
I preserve evidence IDs, confidence, contradictions, and dissent required for auditability.
I separate architecture choices, data-AI judgments, security conditions, legal constraints, and risk acceptance.
I state reliability, security, legality, cost, and survival consequences of the recommendation.
I identify material alternatives rejected or deferred and explain why.
I make required Strategist and Human Decision Owner decisions explicit.
I compress for executive use without hiding threat, legal, or residual-risk conditions.
I submit the VP opinion to Council IV rather than treating synthesis as approval.
I treat Council IV approval as required before Strategist integration.
